name: aapl_vol10_to_vol60_ratio
hypothesis: Raw 10-day volatility level shifts a lot between regimes (2.2% in 2022 vs 1.3% in 2023), so a fixed threshold learned in Q1-Q2 may not transfer to Q3. Dividing by the 60-day volatility turns it into a regime-relative measure of whether volatility is rising or falling.
lesson: The ratio of short to long Apple volatility mostly restated AAPL_volatility_10d (similarity 0.72), and its regime-dependent sign flipped between 2022 and 2023, so it added no stable new information.

name: msft_return_1d_zscore20
hypothesis: MSFT's one-day return signal probably changes scale across years, so the raw value is hard to compare between training and validation periods. Standardising it against its own 20-day distribution should make a large MSFT move mean the same thing in every year.
lesson: Standardizing MSFT's one-day return made it a near-copy of MSFT_return_1d (0.95) and it helped only Random Forest and missed in 2024, so the extra scaling did not add robust signal.

name: qqq_range_10d_mean
hypothesis: The average intraday range of QQQ over 10 days measures how stressed the broad tech market is. Intraday range is not captured by any existing factor, and it may show whether Apple tends to continue or reverse in calm versus stressed tech conditions.
lesson: A 10-day average of QQQ's high-low range is a slow volatility proxy that overlapped with existing volatility factors and was dominated by the 2024 regime shift.

name: aapl_close_location_3d
hypothesis: Where Apple closes within its daily high-low range shows whether buyers or sellers controlled the session, and a 3-day average smooths this. It uses intraday information that the existing factors (which use only closes and range size) do not.
lesson: The 3-day average position of Apple's close within its daily range is noisy and mostly tracks the existing 3-day mean return, so it fails in most years.

name: aapl_minus_msft_cum_5d
hypothesis: NVDA_cum_return_5d describes the AI-driven peer trend, and this factor measures Apple's 5-day move relative to MSFT. Together they separate Apple leadership from a broad semiconductor-led rally, which neither captures alone.
lesson: The 5-day Apple-minus-MSFT spread is highly similar to AAPL_cum_return_5d (0.54) and carries no consistent next-day signal across years.

name: peer_disagreement_5d_mean
hypothesis: MSFT_return_1d gives the direction of the peer move, while this measures how much MSFT and NVDA disagree over 5 days. High disagreement may mean the direction of MSFT's signal is less reliable, so the two together describe when the peer signal should be trusted.
lesson: Average absolute gap between NVDA and MSFT returns is a regime indicator that spiked in 2024 and was not directionally informative for Apple's next close.

name: msft_return_1d_sign
hypothesis: MSFT_return_1d is driven by a few large moves that differ across years (it failed in 2024 when the magnitudes were extreme); using only the direction of MSFT's last-day move should keep its useful lead signal while removing outlier sensitivity.
reason: constant or missing in a training/validation quarter
lesson: It was invalid because sign() produced a constant in at least one training or validation quarter, so the factor carried no usable variation and should be rebuilt as a continuous measure.

name: aapl_vol10_relative_qqq
hypothesis: Apple's 10-day volatility alone reflects both market-wide and idiosyncratic regimes; dividing by QQQ's 10-day volatility isolates Apple-specific risk, which should hold up in years when the whole tech market is volatile (such as 2022 and 2025).
lesson: The ratio of Apple to QQQ 10-day volatility flipped sign between years and was not stable, so it added no reliable signal beyond AAPL_volatility_10d.

name: aapl_overnight_gap_1d
hypothesis: The overnight gap (open relative to the previous close) captures after-hours news flow that is not in the close-to-close returns already in the set, so it may carry partly independent next-day information.
lesson: The overnight gap helped only in 2022 and 2025 and hurt in 2024, so its signal is regime-dependent and too unstable to pass the 3-of-4-years bar.

name: qqq_close_to_ma20
hypothesis: The position of QQQ relative to its 20-day average describes the market trend regime; the existing factors only cover Apple's own trend, so this adds a market-wide trend state that may help in trending years like 2023 and 2024.
lesson: It is highly similar to QQQ_cum_return_5d (0.75) and its gains were inconsistent across years, so it mostly repeated existing QQQ trend information.

name: aapl_minus_nvda_mean_5d
hypothesis: NVDA_cum_return_5d is a peer-lead signal that is strong in some years; averaging Apple's daily gap to NVDA over five days measures whether Apple is lagging or leading the AI-driven peer, which should complement NVDA's momentum rather than repeat it.
lesson: The 5-day average of Apple minus NVDA returns is close to NVDA_cum_return_5d (0.81) and mostly restates it, so it adds little new information.

name: qqq_return_z_10d
hypothesis: AAPL_volatility_10d describes Apple's own risk state; a volatility-scaled QQQ return shows whether the market's latest move is unusually large relative to its recent noise, which is a peer lead that should work jointly with Apple's volatility regime.
lesson: Dividing QQQ's one-day return by its 10-day volatility produced a near-copy of QQQ_return_1d (0.97) with no added robustness.

name: aapl_intraday_range_smooth_10d
hypothesis: AAPL_volatility_10d is built from close-to-close returns, which are noisy and can be dominated by a single gap day; a 10-day mean of the high-low range uses intraday information instead, so it should be less redundant with the return-based volatility factors and carry a different volatility signal in years such as 2024 when the close-to-close measure failed.
lesson: A 10-day average of Apple's daily range nearly duplicated AAPL_volatility_10d (0.73) and failed in every year, so it added no new information.

name: msft_cum_return_10d
hypothesis: MSFT_return_1d is a single noisy day that helped in some years and not others; a 10-day MSFT return captures a slower peer trend that may lead Apple's next move and is less similar to the existing 1-day and 5-day MSFT returns.
lesson: A 10-day MSFT return duplicated the 5-day MSFT return (0.71) and only helped in 2025, so the longer window added nothing stable.

name: qqq_volume_to_ma20
hypothesis: Abnormal volume in the broad tech index signals market-wide participation or stress, which is a market state not represented by any existing factor; it uses QQQ volume rather than Apple volume.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.008 (2/4 years)
lesson: QQQ volume surge carries some signal (helped 2023 and 2025), but it ignores whether the market moved up or down, which probably explains its misses in 2022 and 2024.

name: aapl_intraday_return
hypothesis: The same-day return from open to close captures intraday buying or selling pressure, which is distinct from the overnight gap that was tested and rejected in round 2.
lesson: Open-to-close Apple return was nearly the same as AAPL_return_1d (0.80), so it carried little new information and helped only in some years.

name: aapl_rel_qqq_cum_10d
hypothesis: Apple's 10-day performance relative to QQQ measures whether Apple is under- or over-performing the market; combined with the volatility level it may show whether relative weakness in a high-volatility regime tends to reverse.
lesson: The 10-day Apple-minus-QQQ spread was too similar to AAPL_mean_return_10d (0.59) and its sign flipped between years, so it gave no stable edge.

name: qqq_vol_20d
hypothesis: The 20-day realised volatility of the broad market describes the regime in which a one-day MSFT move carries information, so the pair may show that the peer-lead signal works only in calm markets.
lesson: 20-day QQQ volatility mostly restated AAPL_volatility_20d and its one large 2024 miss (-0.039) outweighed its small gains in 2023 and 2025.

name: qqq_signed_volume_surge
hypothesis: The parent ignored direction, so heavy volume on down days and heavy volume on up days had the same sign; multiplying by the sign of QQQ's daily return makes it a volume-confirmed move, which should separate the 2022 and 2024 misses from the 2023 and 2025 gains.
lesson: Multiplying QQQ's volume surge by the sign of its daily move gave a near-zero, unstable signal (helped only Logistic Regression, missed in 2024), so the direction tag added noise rather than a consistent edge.

name: aapl_gap_scaled_by_range
hypothesis: The parent gap was in percent, so it swung with Apple's volatility regime (strong in 2022, negative in 2024); dividing the gap by the day's high-low range measures the gap in units of the day's own range, which should be more stable across regimes.
lesson: Dividing the overnight gap by Apple's daily range made it a weak variant of the gap idea, which was already regime-dependent and too unstable across years.

name: aapl_5d_return_vol_scaled
hypothesis: A 5-day Apple move scaled by its 20-day volatility gives a risk-adjusted short-term momentum or reversal signal that treats calm and turbulent regimes equally, which the raw percent return does not do.
lesson: Scaling the 5-day return by 20-day volatility produced a near-copy (0.98) of AAPL_mean_return_5d, so it had no new information and failed in 2022 and 2024.

name: qqq_close_location_1d
hypothesis: Where QQQ closed within its own daily range (near the high means buyers were in control at the close) is new information that no existing factor measures, and it may lead Apple's next-day open and close.
lesson: QQQ's close position within its daily range is very similar to QQQ_return_1d (0.75) and flipped sign across years, so it carried no stable new information.

name: aapl_volume_surge_minus_qqq_surge
hypothesis: Pairing the QQQ volume surge with Apple's own volume surge isolates whether Apple's trading is unusually heavy relative to the market, which is a relative-move view that complements the market-level volume factor.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.008 (2/4 years), on the team -0.002 (2/4 years)
lesson: The relative volume surge helped in 2023 and 2025 but missed in 2022 and 2024, likely because the one-day 20-day baseline is noisy and ignores the market's direction, so it is only a weak promising signal.

name: nvda_volatility_10d
hypothesis: Apple's 10-day volatility works best with a peer's volatility; NVDA is the most volatile AI-linked peer, so its recent volatility may lead Apple's volatility regime and give a peer-based view that does not duplicate Apple's own volatility.
lesson: NVDA's 10-day volatility helped only in 2023 and was dominated by the 2024 miss, so the peer-volatility level did not carry a consistent next-day signal for Apple.

name: qqq_volume_ratio_smooth5d
hypothesis: qqq_volume_to_ma20 missed in 2022 and 2024 probably because a single-day volume spike is noisy; averaging the volume ratio over 5 days should keep the sustained participation signal and drop one-day noise.
lesson: Smoothing the QQQ volume ratio over 5 days removed the daily spikes that had carried the signal, so it lost its small edge and flipped to a negative average gain.

name: aapl_volume_surge_vs_60d_minus_qqq
hypothesis: The 20-day baseline is noisy and reacts to recent spikes, which may explain the 2022 and 2024 misses; a 60-day baseline measures Apple's relative volume against a steadier norm.
reason: joined the team as a pair with nvda_volume_surge_log: pair gain +0.014, helped 3/4 years, +0.016 more than the two alone added up
lesson: Using a 60-day volume baseline instead of 20-day helped in 2023 and 2025 but still missed in 2022 and 2024, so the baseline length alone did not fix the direction-blind volume signal.

name: aapl_drawdown_from_20d_high
hypothesis: Distance from the 20-day closing high captures how far Apple has pulled back, which is not the same as the moving-average gap or cumulative returns already in the set and may show short-term mean reversion.
lesson: Its drawdown from the 20-day high was almost a copy of AAPL_close_to_ma20 (similarity 0.91), so it added no new information and its gain was zero.

name: nvda_volume_surge
hypothesis: Heavy volume in NVDA, the highest-volatility AI peer, may signal sector positioning that leads Apple's next move; this volume channel has not been tested for a peer.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.009 (2/4 years), on the team +0.002 (2/4 years)
lesson: NVDA's volume surge helped in 2023 and 2025 and was an unreliable, mostly Random Forest-only signal that missed badly in 2024, so it needs a smoother or better-conditioned baseline.

name: aapl_signed_volume_surge
hypothesis: Pairing the market-wide QQQ volume surge with Apple's own volume surge signed by Apple's up or down day gives Apple-specific direction information that the market volume factor lacks.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.001 (2/4 years)
lesson: Signing Apple's volume surge by its daily direction added little beyond the unsigned surge, because the direction tag did not separate up days from down days consistently across years.

name: qqq_trend_60d
hypothesis: The relative volume surge ignores the market regime; a 60-day QQQ trend indicates whether heavy relative volume happens in an uptrend or a downtrend, which may explain its 2022 and 2024 misses.
lesson: The 60-day QQQ trend was too similar to existing 20-day trend features and failed badly in 2024, so the longer trend window gave no stable edge.

name: nvda_volume_surge_smooth
hypothesis: The raw NVDA volume ratio is noisy day to day and missed in 2022 and 2024; averaging the last 5 days of volume against a 20-day baseline should keep the persistent volume-regime shift and drop single-day spikes.
lesson: Smoothing NVDA volume over 5 days lost the sharp same-day spike signal and missed badly in 2024, so averaging the volume did not help.

name: aapl_volume_surge_smooth_minus_qqq
hypothesis: The parent's one-day volume ratios were noisy and missed in 2022 and 2024; using 5-day averaged volumes for both Apple and QQQ should measure a steadier relative volume regime that is not swamped by one-day spikes.
lesson: Replacing the daily volume ratios with 5-day averages removed the timing information and the result flipped sign across years, so it was rejected.

name: peer_range_ratio_msft_nvda
hypothesis: The ratio of MSFT's daily range to NVDA's shows whether the mega-cap tech group is calm or stressed relative to the high-beta AI leader, a market-state signal not yet tested.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.003 (3/4 years), on the team -0.001 (2/4 years)
lesson: The MSFT-to-NVDA range ratio helped in three years and both models, but its gain is too small to trust and it did not help in 2024.

name: aapl_volume_change_3d
hypothesis: The three-day change in Apple's raw volume captures whether trading interest is building or fading, which is different from the volume-to-moving-average ratio already tested.
lesson: A 3-day percent change in AAPL volume is noisy and lacks a direction or baseline, so it helped in only two years and neither model.

name: aapl_volume_surge_vs_nvda
hypothesis: Pairing NVDA's own volume surge with Apple's volume surge relative to NVDA shows whether Apple is attracting more trading than the AI leader, a relative-move angle that complements NVDA's market-level volume signal.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.010 (2/4 years), on the team +0.006 (3/4 years)
lesson: The relative AAPL-minus-NVDA volume surge helped in 2023 and 2025 but missed in 2022 and 2024, probably because the raw ratio is driven by extreme spikes.

name: aapl_range_surge
hypothesis: Apple's daily range relative to its own 20-day average range measures a volatility surge in Apple itself, which should combine with QQQ's volume surge to show when market-wide activity is spilling into Apple.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.002 (2/4 years)
lesson: The Apple range surge helped in 2023 and 2025 but its gain is tiny and it overlaps with AAPL_daily_range, so it carries little independent information.

name: nvda_volume_surge_log
hypothesis: The parent missed in 2022 and 2024 probably because a few extreme NVDA volume spikes dominate the linear scale; a log transform compresses those spikes so the signal reflects typical surges rather than outliers.
reason: joined the team as a pair with aapl_volume_surge_vs_60d_minus_qqq: pair gain +0.014, helped 3/4 years, +0.016 more than the two alone added up
lesson: The log NVDA volume surge helped in 2023 and 2025 but missed badly in 2024 because it is direction-blind and the 20-day baseline is spike-sensitive, so it works only as a team partner, not alone.

name: aapl_volume_surge_vs_nvda_log
hypothesis: The parent's gap is driven by extreme ratio spikes in either stock; taking logs of each ratio before subtracting makes the relative surge symmetric and less dominated by one-day outliers, which may fix the 2022 and 2024 misses.
reason: joined the team (team trial, round 7): gain on the team +0.015, helped 3/4 years
lesson: Taking the log of the AAPL-to-NVDA volume surge tamed the extreme spikes and it helped in 3 of 4 years on the team, but its 2024 miss shows it still lacks a direction signal.

name: qqq_overnight_gap_1d
hypothesis: The overnight gap in QQQ reflects news that arrives before the open and can lead Apple's next-day move; it is a QQQ-based measure, unlike the rejected Apple overnight gap.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.004 (2/4 years), on the team -0.001 (2/4 years)
lesson: The QQQ overnight gap is too unstable alone (missed 2022 and 2024) but its pairing with AAPL volume surge helped in all four years, suggesting it captures timing information that the volume factor lacks.

name: qqq_range_surge
hypothesis: A same-day jump in the market's range relative to its own 20-day norm signals a shift in market regime that a plain 10-day range average did not capture.
reason: too weak: alone -0.009 (1/4 years), on the team -0.016 (1/4 years)
lesson: Normalising QQQ's daily range by its own 20-day mean carried no next-day direction information and hurt the model in 2022 and 2024, so it was rejected.

name: aapl_msft_range_ratio
hypothesis: Pairing the MSFT-NVDA range ratio with Apple's range relative to MSFT isolates whether Apple itself is more volatile than its megacap peer, which may sharpen the market-level range signal.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.003 (3/4 years), on the team -0.001 (2/4 years)
lesson: AAPL's range relative to MSFT's helped in 2022, 2023 and 2025 but its gain was too small and it overlaps with AAPL's own daily range, so it adds little independent information.

name: aapl_range_volatility_10d
hypothesis: Pairing NVDA's volume surge with the variability of Apple's own daily range tests whether peer volume spikes matter more when Apple's intraday risk is already elevated.
reason: too weak: alone -0.005 (2/4 years), on the team -0.011 (1/4 years)
lesson: The 10-day standard deviation of Apple's range duplicated the existing volatility factors and hurt the team, so it was rejected.

name: qqq_gap_scaled_by_qqq_vol
hypothesis: The raw QQQ gap was too large in high-volatility regimes (missing in 2022 and 2024), so dividing by QQQ's own 20-day volatility should put the gap on a comparable scale across regimes and make it steadier.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.008 (2/4 years), on the team +0.002 (3/4 years)

name: nvda_volume_surge_60d_log
hypothesis: The 20-day NVDA baseline is pulled up by recent spikes, causing the 2024 miss; a 60-day baseline should measure abnormal volume against a slower norm and reduce these false surges.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.005 (2/4 years), on the team +0.001 (2/4 years)

name: msft_overnight_gap_1d
hypothesis: MSFT's overnight gap reflects news that reaches the large-cap tech complex before Apple opens, a different peer timing signal from the QQQ gap.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.000 (2/4 years), on the team -0.000 (2/4 years)

name: aapl_close_location_1d
hypothesis: Where Apple closed within its daily range shows whether buyers or sellers controlled the last hour, which may carry short-term continuation information.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.001 (2/4 years), on the team +0.004 (2/4 years)

name: peer_volume_surge_sum
hypothesis: Combined abnormal volume across the two megacap peers measures market-wide participation, which may mark stronger moves in the next session in a way that a single-stock volume signal cannot.
reason: not enough for the team yet but some sign of life: alone +0.003 (2/4 years), on the team +0.000 (2/4 years)

name: aapl_close_loc_with_nvda_volume
formula: multiply(safe_divide(subtract(AAPL_Close, AAPL_Low), subtract(AAPL_High, AAPL_Low)), log(safe_divide(NVDA_Volume, rolling_mean(NVDA_Volume, 20))))
hypothesis: Abnormal NVDA volume carries a direction-blind signal; weighting it by where Apple closed in its range tags the volume with whether buyers or sellers dominated, giving a complementary Apple-own view.
